title: Constantin Brancoveanu and Constantin Cantacuzino to Hetman Sieniawski, 1709-1714, in the Wallachian chancellery key (DECODE R7468-R7474, R7477-R7480, R7483)

documents.shelfmark: Archiwum Narodowe w Krakowie, Zbiór Dzieduszyckich 26/32 nr 13 pp. 1-28, 35-49 and nr 5 pp. 9-10; DECODE R7468-R7474, R7477-R7480, R7483
documents.route: Constantin Brâncoveanu and Constantin Cantacuzino (Wallachia) -> Hetman Adam Mikołaj Sieniawski

plaintext.source: Kaczka, Danubius XXX (2012), nos. IV, V, VIII, XIII, XVII, XIX, XX, XXI, XXIII, XXV, XXVI, printed from these originals with key A (fn. 21); interlinear glosses on the 1709 letters and on R7473

transcription.source: only R7473 p. 17, ten lines, checked against key A, the gloss and Kaczka's text (sien/R7473_check.txt); the page map is sien/map.md

system.summary: The Wallachian chancellery's key for Polish letters (Kaczka 2012 fn. 21, after Mares 1987): a two-digit numerical substitution (a=19, b=60, c=66 ...) with a few code numbers (900 = August); written dot-separated (R7473) or run together (R7468-R7472).
system.sibling_key: Kaczka 2012 fn. 21 (key A), used to check R7473
system.notes: Split 14 Oct 2026: the other systems of the old entry are separate entries.

prior_solution.where: Kaczka, Danubius XXX (2012), nos. IV, V, VIII, XIII, XVII, XIX, XX, XXI, XXIII, XXV, XXVI, with key A

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie supplied and the target assigned in a brief (catalogue entry 333). No target-specific intervention.
tools: DECODE JSON API and filesrv download

solution.what: DECODE metadata for R7460-R7507 by API; 130 images of R7462-R7507 with the session cookie; no key or decryption file on any record.
Neighbouring records R7460-R7467 (ASang 85/3 keys, Krakow_UNK_1/2) and R7501-R7507 (Wąsowicz-Lubomirski, key R7501) checked as keys for the group.

Kaczka, Danubius XXX (2012) prints the Brâncoveanu/Cantacuzino letters of nr 13 and nr 5 from these originals with keys A and B; nothing on the Schenck letters, R7475, R7476, R7481-R7482, R7484-R7485.
R7473 p. 17, ten lines decoded with Kaczka's key A agree with the interlinear gloss and his printed text.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 from sieniawski1708 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the Vienna-Schenck letters are schenck1706; the Sieniawski letters are one entry per key: key A (sieniawski1708), key B (turculet1709), the R7475 table (r7475), the Chomentowski syllabary (chomentowski1713).
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked Kaczka 2012 by URL and the R7473 ten-line check; the other letters not transcribed

Verification 5 (plain bar, 23 Oct 2026): the letters are Polish (explicit-hole bar); the reading is Kaczka's edition, checked over ten lines (explicit 0.8). Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py; all entries keep read; reading_review notes record both scores.

outcome.method_basis: Kaczka printed these letters from the originals with the chancellery key in 2012; ten lines of R7473 decoded with his key agree with the interlinear gloss and his text.
outcome.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from the joint entry. Sample check only: the letters were not transcribed here; their text is Kaczka's. DECODE lists them as N/A with no decipherment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Kaczka 2012 prints the full text of all twelve; nothing measured here beyond R7473 p. 17 (sien/R7473_check.txt)

credits.note: Danubius XXX prints twelve of the Sieniawski-group letters and the Wallachian chancellery key (A) and the Turculeț key (B); used to read and check

texts.summary: Letters of Constantin Brâncoveanu, prince of Wallachia, and Constantin Cantacuzino to Hetman Adam Mikołaj Sieniawski, 1709-1714, in Polish in the Wallachian chancellery key, with contemporary interlinear decipherments.
texts.note: Decryption: M. W. Kaczka, Danubius XXX (2012), pp. 101-140, a modern edition, linked, not copied. The project transcribed and decoded only the first ten lines of R7473 (sien/R7473_check.txt); the other letters are not transcribed.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (plain bar, VERIFY5_BRIEF): Polish of 1709-14, not French: the explicit-hole share is the bar. The reading is Kaczka's printed edition (Danubius 2012, linked, not copied); the project's check of R7473 p. 17 (sien/R7473_check.txt) matches it word for word over ten lines, the key-A decode lines explicit 0.8 (4/5; the hole a part-word at the line break). Keeps read (read from existing decipherment).
